summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style profile and statistics infobox for Curtis Granderson, an outfielder for the Toronto Blue Jays, wearing No. 18. It gives his birth details, batting and throwing hands, and MLB debut with the Detroit Tigers on September 13, 2004. It also lists his career statistics through July 7, 2018, the teams he played for from 2004 to the present, and his major awards and All-Star selections.
one_line: Curtis Granderson is a left-batting MLB outfielder who played for six teams, including the Detroit Tigers, Yankees, Mets and Blue Jays, and earned three All-Star selections.
key_facts: Curtis Granderson was born March 16, 1981, in Blue Island, Illinois.
Curtis Granderson bats left and throws right.
Curtis Granderson made his MLB debut on September 13, 2004, for the Detroit Tigers.
Through July 7, 2018, Curtis Granderson had a batting average of .252.
Through July 7, 2018, Curtis Granderson had 1,711 hits, 328 home runs, 893 runs batted in, 1,145 runs and 152 stolen bases.
Curtis Granderson played for the Detroit Tigers from 2004 to 2009.
Curtis Granderson played for the New York Yankees from 2010 to 2013.
Curtis Granderson played for the New York Mets from 2014 to 2017.
Curtis Granderson played for the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2017.
Curtis Granderson has played for the Toronto Blue Jays since 2018.
Curtis Granderson was a 3-time All-Star, selected in 2009, 2011 and 2012.
Curtis Granderson won the Silver Slugger Award in 2011 and was the AL RBI leader that year.
Curtis Granderson won the Roberto Clemente Award in 2016.
Curtis Granderson won the Marvin Miller Man of the Year Award twice, in 2009 and 2016.
